doc.title: Jerry Jerome interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Lester Young's tinkerbell and the Famous Door
summary: Lester Young rigged a bell to ring when someone goofed; the band played the Famous Door where Jerry once took Dinah Shore to dinner.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Did Lester Young have any peculiarities that you noticed at the time?

Well it was a cute thing. When the Basie band came up to New York, this was the finished band, this was not like the band that was in Kansas City, this was a full band, they had full brass, full saxes. And Lester and Herschel Evans were playing in this band. And Lester had a cute thing. He had a string tied between his stand and the next, the third alto stand, and in the middle of it was a little bell, like a tinkerbell. If anybody in the band goofed, he’d ring it. And it was the funniest thing. Somebody’d be playing and with his ear he’d hear something. And the crowd didn’t get it but everybody who knew would get hysterical you know.
That’s great. And he would be holding his horn at that strange—
Oh yes, and sometimes wearing a hat, most times wearing a hat.
They made quite a splash at the what was it, something Door?

That was where that happened, that specifically. I had taken Dinah Shore there for dinner, for a date, we had a date there at that time. We were both single at the time. And she thought the food was the best thing. Dinah was a little heavy at the time, but she was coming along.
